scarcity-s2.title: Juniper Ridge Bike Co. starts up
scarcity-s2.html: Ana Ruiz quits her job and puts her savings into a bike repair company, Juniper Ridge Bike Co. She rents a lot beside a river and uses its water to wash bikes. economic-systems-s2.title: Tessaly's winter coats
economic-systems-s2.html: In the invented country of Tessaly, a central planning office decides how many coats the state-owned clothing factories make each year and sets the price of every coat. This year the office ordered 2 million summer jackets and 1 million winter coats. By December, stores have racks of unsold summer jackets, while winter coats are gone within days of each delivery and long lines form whenever a truck arrives. The price of a winter coat stays where the office set it.

marginal-analysis-s3.title: Pellham Games and its unfinished game
marginal-analysis-s3.html: Pellham Games, an invented studio, has already spent $200,000 building a new game, money it cannot get back. Finishing the game would cost another $50,000. The studio expects to take in $80,000 from sales once the game is finished. A manager says, "We have spent so much that we cannot quit now," and another says, "We will never earn back the $200,000, so we should stop."

items.q: What does scarcity mean in economics?
options: A good has run out in stores
People with low incomes face it, but others do not
Resources are limited while wants are unlimited
Prices are higher than people would like

items.q: A billionaire has more money than she could ever spend. Does she face scarcity?
options: Yes: her time is still limited
No: with enough money nothing is scarce
No: scarcity is a problem that firms face, not people
Yes, but just in years when prices are rising

items.q: Which of these is capital, as a factor of production?

The baker's skill at decorating cakes
The farmland the wheat grows on
An oven in a bakery

items.q: The shop chooses the wedding invitations. What is the opportunity cost of that choice, in dollars?

mistakes.why: That adds both jobs, but the press could print only one of them. The opportunity cost is the single next-best job.

items.q: What are Rosa's explicit costs for the summer, in dollars?

mistakes.why: That adds the pay and the truck rent she gives up, which she never pays out. Those are implicit costs; explicit costs are only the money she spends.

mistakes.why: The truck rent she gives up counts too: using her family's truck means not renting it out for $500.

items.q: How many lessons a month give Jamal the largest net benefit?

items.q: Make it specific: explain how many slices Nadia should buy at $2.50 each. Fill in each blank.

specific.frame: She buys a slice while its ___ is at least its ___. The 3rd slice is worth $3.00 and the 4th only ___, so she buys ___ slices.

rule.label: What she compares
options: marginal benefit
total benefit

why.1: Total benefit rises with every slice; the choice depends on what ONE MORE slice adds.

cost.label: Against what
options: price of $2.50
sunk cost

why.1: Nothing has been spent yet; each slice costs its $2.50 price.
$14.00 is the total for four slices; the 4th slice alone is worth $2.00.
The 4th and 5th slices are worth less than $2.50 each.

specific.model: She buys a slice while its marginal benefit is at least its price of $2.50. The 3rd slice is worth $3.00, more than $2.50, and the 4th only $2.00, less than $2.50, so she buys 3 slices.
